title: OpenAI admits a billing error, and your GPT-6.2 usage now burns faster
excerpt: OpenAI blames a launch mistake and offers one saved reset
content_html:
Published Nov 27, 2026, 5:39 AM EST

Anvinraj Valiyathara is a technology journalist with more than 15 years of experience covering the global tech industry. He has published over 20,000 articles across outlets including GizmoChina, Croma Unboxed, MySmartPrice, Pricebaba, Playfuldroid, BGR India, Free Press Journal, and IBTimes.

He specializes in tech news, leaks, smartphones, consumer electronics, and emerging technologies and has reviewed everything from phones and tablets to wearables.

Anvinraj is known for accuracy and for turning complex technical developments into clear, accessible stories. Outside work, he's a Formula 1 fan who loves to travel.

OpenAI says it made a billing mistake when GPT-6.2 launched, undercounting how much usage Astra and Sol consumed. Now that the issue has been fixed, the same tasks use more of your plan's allowance, and OpenAI is adding one banked reset as an apology.

Thibault "Tibo" Sottiaux, who works on Codecs and ChatGPT at OpenAI, said in a post on November 26 that a billing error incorrectly discounted Astra and Sol usage for most users. Compared with the launch week, you will now reach your limits 40% faster on GPT-6.2 Astra and 25% faster on Sol. This means your allowance will run out sooner, while subscription prices remain unchanged.

GPT-6.2 launched on November 17 with two models. Astra is OpenAI's frontier model designed for harder, more complex projects. It is the successor to GPT-6 Astra, which streamed Minecraft for 141 hours in September. Sol, meanwhile, is the more affordable model intended for everyday tasks. At launch, OpenAI made both models available to Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu subscribers through ChatGPT Work and Codex.

Astra takes the biggest hit

Sol is affected too, but other models remain unchanged

OpenAI's launch post pitched both models as a way to get more done within your usage limits. Both run in ChatGPT Work and Codex, which share one usage allowance. Other models weren't affected, and OpenAI says it won't charge users for the difference in past usage. It still expects Astra and Sol to handle more work than GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, but hasn't disclosed how many tasks each plan now covers.

Heavy agent features, such as Codex Goals, continue to work through multi-step projects. That's the kind of workload where usage limits matter most.

How the free reset works

OpenAI is adding the reset for everyone on Go, Plus, Pro, and Business plans. The banked reset sits in your account and doesn't refresh anything until you redeem it, according to OpenAI's Codex reset documentation. It only works when at least one covered allowance has less than 80% remaining.

A full reset restores Go's monthly allowance, the five-hour and weekly allowances on Plus and Business Standard, and the weekly allowances on Pro 100, Pro 200, and Pro 500.

OpenAI hasn't said when the reset expires. BleepingComputer checked its own account and found that it expires a month after being added. The reset doesn't increase your plan's limits and is separate from your regular scheduled usage refresh. Usage limits have already been a sore point. In late September, OpenAI gave some Pro 200 subscribers 62,500 free credits after planning to cut that plan's allowance.
